note: A different rubric from rounds 10 and 11. Those scored code quality (7.6 / 7.0). This scores whether the system can be deployed, operated, diagnosed and recovered. The lower numbers are not a regression: SA-R11-01 and SA-R11-02 were both verified closed since round 11, and nothing got worse.

trustweave.verdict: Ready within its stated GA scope

blockers: PR-01 SaaS: no metrics registry, no tracing, no correlation ids, no custom health indicators, no structured logging config
PR-02 SaaS: no infrastructure-as-code; docker-compose is the documented deploy path and hardcodes postgres/admin credentials
PR-03 SaaS: built against eight 1.0.0-SNAPSHOT library dependencies, a version the library has never released
PR-04 SaaS: in-process rate limiter and five uncoordinated @Scheduled jobs; usage-outbox drain has no claim before posting
PR-05 SaaS: integration suite cannot currently run (Docker stalls on PostgreSQL container startup)
PR-06 Library: no artifact signing, SBOM, provenance, or SAST on a published security library
needed_not_blocking: PR-07 SaaS: no retry, backoff or circuit breaker around any external dependency
PR-08 SaaS: fly.toml is stale and non-functional (port 8080 vs app 8081, postgres:// URL the JDBC driver cannot consume, placeholder Keycloak host) and carries a plaintext password
PR-09 Library: 108 swallowed exceptions with no log line; only 37 files use a logging framework across 231k LOC
PR-10 SaaS: retention covers two tables; subject PII not encrypted at rest by the application; no backup or restore procedure
PR-11 SaaS: no ktlint/detekt/spotless, no Dependabot, no npm audit
production_grade_already: docs/api-reference/module-maturity.md states that publishing a JAR does not imply production suitability, tiers every module (8 GA, 12 Experimental, 2 supported-with-provider), and gives per-module test counts including 'Experimental - untested' labels
KmsProviderConfig refuses ephemeral in-memory key providers outside dev/test/local, so issuer keys cannot silently live in heap in production
Schema ownership settled: all profiles run ddl-auto:validate with Flyway authoritative, and FlywayMigrationTest builds from an empty database while deriving expected tables from @Table annotations

SA-R11-01 closed structurally: platform-admin realm role gates operations and metrics in both filter chains and on the controller; TenantAdministration is a single chokepoint requiring admin plus organization access for every user and group lookup
SA-R11-02 closed: Keycloak server URL and admin credentials require explicit environment values
Cross-repository supply chain: CI pins the library by git revision and verifies a source hash, tightened in round 11 with an explicit --revision

Idempotency and bounded work: processed-webhook-event table, usage-event idempotency keys, 57 uses of pagination, batch-bounded purges, a database work lease on the OID4VP path, non-root container user
reference-wallet/README.md states the wallets are not production custody products
recommended_sequence: Restore the Docker environment (PR-05) so the suite, including the migration test, can run
Instrument the service (PR-01): Prometheus registry, MDC filter with request and organization ids, JSON logging, health indicators for Keycloak and billing
Commit the AWS staging design as infrastructure code (PR-02), which also supplies the secret manager and managed Postgres
Cut a real library release (PR-03 + PR-06 + TW-R10-06): validate and freeze the API surface, sign, publish an SBOM, then pin the SaaS to a fixed version
Make the outbox drain safe (PR-04): SKIP LOCKED and a claimed status, then ShedLock and a shared rate limiter
Then the hygiene backlog: ktlint and Dependabot on the SaaS, retries around Keycloak and Accountly, retention for the remaining tables, and the eleven findings carried forward from round 10
correction_to_round_11: SA-R11-03 reported nine corrupted UI strings. The round-11 remediation pass found only three were displayed text; the other six were JSX ternaries (isLoading ? () that the search pattern matched. Verified: the correction is right, and Explain.tsx:72 carries a correct ellipsis. The finding was a third of the size reported.
method: Static analysis of both working trees, re-verifying the round-11 remediation in source before assessing readiness across build and dependency configuration, deployment and container definitions, Spring profiles, the observability and health surface, scheduled and concurrent work, data lifecycle, and the projects' own maturity documentation.
limits: Nothing was deployed, started, load-tested or profiled, and no build or test run was executed; the judgement is drawn from configuration and code, not observed behaviour. Both trees carry uncommitted modifications; this reflects the working tree, not HEAD. PR-05 rests on the round-11 remediation report's account of the Docker failure rather than an independent reproduction. Capacity figures (512 MB, one shared vCPU) are noted as unvalidated rather than scored.
